# Visual management audit

Whether a visual board's zones are actually staying current weeks after it was designed — the sustainment audit's shape, applied to a visual board instead of a kaizen event.

Family: Visual management · Format: .xlsx · Domain: core

## What it is

A visual board designed once and never checked tends to go stale exactly where it matters. This audit is the sustainment audit's exact shape, applied to a visual board: restate what the board was supposed to keep current, get a checklist of specific zones and practices to verify, and see honestly which are still holding.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- A visual board has been in place long enough to check whether its zones are actually being kept current.
- You want to catch a zone that's gone stale, or one whose update ownership never got assigned, before the board loses the team's trust.
- You want to verify the team is genuinely using the board, not just walking past it.

Not when:

- The board was just designed — give it real time to settle into use before auditing it.

## How to fill it in

- **originalObjective** — What was the visual board supposed to keep current?
- **checks** — Drafted from what the board was supposed to show — verify what's actually still holding.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the checklist actually built.

## What good looks like

The example below audits the tier-7 visual board thirty-five days after it was designed — including whether the escalation-matrix zone's originally-unassigned update owner has since been named.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://www.katafacts.com/katas/visual-management-audit

## Common mistakes

- **Auditing a board that's never actually been used by the team.** — There's nothing to check if the board was designed but never adopted — that's a rollout problem, not a sustainment one.
- **Treating a stale zone as a minor issue rather than raising it.** — A board with even one stale zone starts losing the team's trust in all of it — small gaps are worth closing quickly.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Visual board design guide** — The board's own zone specifications and update owners are exactly what this audit checks against reality.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding how much time to give a board before auditing it
- Deciding what to do about a zone that's flagged at risk

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting specific, verifiable checks from a description of what the board was supposed to keep current
- Drafting the narrative from the checklist actually built

Drudgery — automated:

- Tallying how many practices are still holding
- Identifying which zones are at risk
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
